collection.source_input: US8300325B2, the prescription table transcribed in this batch's brief (the brief's table 1 of 8; the publication's own Example 3, confirmed against its conditional-expression table): a 12-surface prescription, surfaces 1-4, the stop, 6-12
collection.redistribution: public patent document; the prescription numbers are transcribed as facts, no source asset is redistributed
collection.attribution: US8300325B2, Olympus Medical Systems Corp.; the design is cited by publication number and example

title: Objective lens and endoscope using the same, US8300325B2 example 3 (batch record us8300325b2-ex1)

design.source_reference: US8300325B2 example 3. The brief numbers this table 1 of 8; the publication's own Example 3 label is confirmed, not assumed: the publication's TABLE 1 of conditional expressions gives example 3 as nn 2.100, (vp - vn) 24.68, (f23/f1) 1.556, n1 1.768, n2 1.923, and this surface table is the only one that produces them (surface 9 nd 2.100 with v 30.00, surface 8 v 54.68, surfaces 1 and 3 at 1.768 and 1.923)

aperture_validity.basis: the source marks an aperture stop as its own surface between the second lens (surfaces 3-4) and the third lens (surfaces 6-7); the engine builds it as a plate whose opening (0.20 mm semi-diameter) is smaller than the clear semi-diameters beside it (0.42 mm), so light outside the opening is blocked
aperture_validity.consequence: the record is eligible for stop-dependent evaluation, but no stop-dependent match is claimed
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point, a pupil sample or an illumination measurement), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.56 nm (the d line, the wavelength the source's nd refers to), converted once to vacuum; the batch's d-line vacuum value 587.7220645720764 nm is used so every record of this collection evaluates the same d line
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states nd and vd only, so the Project is evaluated at the d line alone. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; an nd/vd pair does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

comparison.why: the publication states neither an effective focal length nor a back focal length for this example, so the two-quantity rule has no pair to judge. The engine's values are recorded under engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts and no verdict is claimed

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states no effective focal length in millimetres for this table. Its TABLE 1 of conditional expressions prints 'a focal length of the entire system' as a normalised 1.000 for every example, which is a design target, not a measured focal length, so no source-stated first-order value exists to compare against

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point

paraxial_working_f_number.definition: Reciprocal of twice the admitted axial marginal ray's reduced image angle.

field.note: the publication's surface table for this example states no field angle, object height or image height, and the publication's conditional-expression table carries none either, so no field value is asserted

model_glasses.name: G176800
model_glasses.basis: the source states nd 1.768 and v 72.23 only; two numbers do not define a dispersion curve, so the material is a constant index at the stated nd and no dispersion is claimed

model_glasses.name: G192300
model_glasses.basis: the source states nd 1.923 and v 18.90 only; constant index at the stated nd, no dispersion claimed

model_glasses.name: G172900
model_glasses.basis: the source states nd 1.729 and v 54.68 only; constant index at the stated nd, no dispersion claimed. Used on surfaces 6 and 8 (the third lens and the positive element of the cemented pair)

model_glasses.name: G210000
model_glasses.basis: the source states nd 2.100 and v 30.00 only; constant index at the stated nd, no dispersion claimed. This is the negative element of the cemented pair, the nn of conditional expression (1)

model_glasses.name: G151600
model_glasses.basis: the source states nd 1.516 and v 64.14 only; constant index at the stated nd, no dispersion claimed. The plane-parallel cover glass, surfaces 11-12

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.

catalog_comparisons.note: cross-check only, not substituted. The source's 1.768 / 72.23 has no exact catalog entry
cross-check only. No catalog glass is close in both nd and vd: the nearest by index is 13 Abbe units away, which is why no substitution could stand in for the source's stated pair

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source states no clear aperture, and this table states neither an f-number nor an image height, so the guide's EFL/(2*F#) rule has no F# to use. Semi-diameters were set from the prescription's own geometry: 0.40 mm clear semi-diameter over the front group (0.8 mm clear diameter, the small-diameter class the publication describes), 0.20 mm at the stop so the plate is the smallest aperture in the system, and 0.42-0.55 mm growing toward the image side to carry the off-axis beam onto the cover plate. They set the stop plate and the solid checks and do not enter the first-order values; no f-number is asserted anywhere in this record
the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the engine reaches the plate to the largest outline radius of the unit (0.57 mm, the cover plate's rim), reduced to clear the neighbouring elements

the source states an object distance of 9.756 mm on the object row; the Project places the source there, so the record is finite-conjugate. The paraxial image for that conjugate lands at 6.3218 mm, 0.0038 mm beyond the source's own image plane at 6.318 mm, which is the order of the table's four-decimal rounding
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0

project solids reported no error-severity finding; it reports EDGE_THICKNESS_IMPLAUSIBLE at INFO severity on all five elements, which is expected for a prescription whose glass is 0.5-1.4 mm thick on a 0.8-1.1 mm clear diameter

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length or back focal length in millimetres. Its conditional-expression table prints a normalised focal length of the entire system of 1.000 for every example, a design target that the engine's 1.001729 mm lands 0.17 % above, outside the 1e-5 + 1e-4*scale rule

the transcription is self-consistent with the source: the paraxial image for the source's stated 9.756 mm object distance lands at 6.3218 mm against the source's image plane at 6.318 mm (0.06 % of the total track)
the example number is the publication's own Example 3, not the brief's index 1: see design.source_reference for the conditional-expression values that confirm it
the source states no aperture at all for this table, so every system-aperture field is left out rather than inferred; the stop opening in the CSV is a geometric choice, not a stated aperture
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline. Recompute it from the committed record.json after parsing the JSON, not from the file's bytes.
